chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, peace be upon them, that he said:

"When a man enters upon you desiring your family and your wealth, then strike him first if you are able, for the thief is a combatant of God and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), and whatever of his property follows you, it is mine."

key_terms.اللِّصَّ: The thief (specifically in the context of theft by entry)
key_terms.فَمَا تَبِعَكَ: And whatever follows you (i.e., what you take from him)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for striking a thief who enters your home?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt establishes the principle of preemptive self-defense against a thief (al-liṣṍ) who enters one's home with intent to seize family and wealth, classifying them as a 'combatant of God' (muḥārib). It emphasizes the homeowner's right to strike first if capable, linking the act to the Quranic concept of *hirābah*, and declares that any property taken by the homeowner becomes the Imam's share (khums), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view on the disposition of stolen goods.
